title: The tree of life
examples: How do scientists use the tree of life?
What does 'common ancestry' really mean for animals?
Can you show me where humans fit on the tree?

explain.say: The tree of life shows how all living things are related.
All life shares a common ancestor at some point in the past.
The branches on the tree show groups that split from a common ancestor.
Scientists group life into major kingdoms based on shared traits.
A concrete example is comparing a plant and an animal.
In everyday life, the tree helps us understand medicine.

faq.q: What is the tree of life exactly?
faq.a: It is a diagram showing the evolutionary relationships between different groups of organisms. It helps scientists see how life has changed over time.
asks: What does the tree show about life?

faq.q: Does 'common ancestry' mean everything is related?
faq.a: Yes, it means that all life on Earth shares a single, distant ancestor. It does not mean they look similar now.
Traditionally, life is grouped into several major kingdoms. The main ones include animals, plants, and fungi.
asks: What are the main groups of life?

faq.a: No, the branches represent different lines of evolution that have been changing at different rates. Some lines are much older than others.
asks: Do all groups evolve at the same speed?

faq.q: Do humans belong to a specific kingdom?
faq.a: Yes, humans belong to the Animal Kingdom, which is one of the major groups on the tree. We are related to other animals.

facts: The tree of life illustrates evolutionary relationships among species.
Common ancestry suggests that all life descended from a single source.
Life is broadly categorized into major kingdoms, like Animalia and Plantae.
Branches on the tree show lineages that have diverged over time.

quiz.say: If a group of organisms shares a common ancestor, it means:

options.show: They descended from a common source.
options.say: They descended from a common source.

options.show: They live in the same place.
options.say: They live in the same place.

options.show: They were created at the same time.
options.say: They were created at the same time.

quiz.why: This shows a shared evolutionary past for the group.

wrong.1: Similarity can be due to chance, not just ancestry.
wrong.2: Location does not prove shared ancestry.
wrong.3: Evolution takes vast amounts of time.

quiz.say: Which kingdom includes organisms that eat other things for energy?
quiz.why: Animals must consume other organisms to get energy.

wrong.0: This group is too varied to give one answer.
wrong.2: Plants make their own food using sunlight.
wrong.3: Fungi absorb nutrients from dead matter.

quiz.say: A diagram showing how life groups split from a shared ancestor is best described as a:
quiz.why: The tree structure perfectly models branching evolution.

wrong.0: Venn diagrams compare overlapping sets, not deep history.
wrong.2: Cycles show repeating processes, not branching history.
wrong.3: A timeline shows events in order, not relationships.
